t: What Food Preservation Performance Database Is All About
title: What Food Preservation Performance Database Is All About
description: Preservation stops the microbes and enzymes that spoil food: canning (Appert, 1810; 121°C pressure for low-acid), freezing (Birdseye, 1920s; speed preserves texture), drying (water activity below 0.85 stops most bacteria), and fermentation (lactic acid drops pH). Each method trades shelf life against nutrition and taste: freeze-drying keeps the most, canning the least. Safety first — low-acid canning done wrong breeds botulism. This database is the complete preservation method: full records with definitions, key facts, procedures, and runnable demo programs, organized on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced.
